newsitem.title: USA: Rail firm seeks finance for U.S. freight line -WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Rail firm seeks finance for U.S. freight line -WSJ.

text.p: Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern Railroad Corp is looking to finance a $1.2 billion freight line would directly compete with two railroad giants for control of the nation's largest coal market, the Wall Street Journal said.
In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said the line would run from the midwest to northeastern Wyoming, going head to head against Union Pacific Corp and Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp.
It also appears to signal a chance for regional and, in some case, start-up companies to compete in an industry dominated by five carriers.
"This is the next step in deregulation," said Brian Routledge, an analyst with Prudential Securities. The smaller lines are "now picking their spots where they can be bigger players."
Dakota, Minnesota & Eastern is currently searching for strategic partners to try to raise the necessary financing.
The Brookings, S.D., company plans to rebuild 650 miles of its own track from Minnesota to Rapid City, S.D., then add an additional 250 miles of track into northeastern Wyoming.
